## Diagnosis before the final round

The gen-8 results map the frontier precisely and identify the one lever that trades favorably:

| signal | α | t(α) | Sharpe | FMB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CapitalStockScaled3YAccruals (base) | −7.4% | −4.62 | −0.582 | −0.90 |
| base × dp/capx amplifier | −6.4% | −4.29 | −0.567 | **−1.76** |
| base weighted 2:1 with dep-adequacy limb | −6.9% | −4.58 | **−0.602** | −1.65 |
| GrossPPE floor (over-flooring) | −6.8% | −4.13 | −0.502 | −0.55 |
| One-year base (no cumulation) | −4.6% | −2.74 | −0.297 | −0.79 |

Four settled facts: (i) the **capital-stock floor plus three-year cumulation** is the alpha engine — removing either costs 3 points of alpha, and over-flooring with gross PPE adds nothing; (ii) the **dp/capx amplifier is the only construction that buys slope cheaply** (+0.86 of t for 1 point of alpha), and it works better multiplicatively than additively; (iii) numerator refinements (tax validation) preserve the alpha but not the slope, so the slope lives in the *investment-inadequacy* dimension, not the accrual-measurement dimension; (iv) the deficit numerator, which owns the archive's strongest slopes (−3.2 to −3.4), has **never been paired with the capital-stock denominator** — the single most informative untested cell.

Final batch: push the amplifier toward bounded forms that should improve monotonicity without discarding tail information (1, 3), settle the additive weighting (2), test the untested numerator×denominator cell (4), and broaden the recognition concept and the coverage-robust measurement (5, 6).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ReplacementShareAmplifiedCapStockAccruals
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent)), RATIO(TS_SUM(dp, 3), TS_SUM(ADD(capx, dp), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accruals accumulated against the productive capital base matter most when gross investment is mostly just depreciation, that is when the replacement share of investment approaches one and no new capacity is being created.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The dp/capx amplifier bought the best slope-for-alpha trade in the archive but is unbounded and explosive for near-zero capex, which plausibly caps its slope contribution at −1.76; replacing it with dp/(capx+dp) keeps the identical economic content — the fraction of gross investment that is mere replacement — while bounding it in [0,1] and keeping it dense. Because the amplifier is now well behaved, the product should be closer to linear in the cross-section, so I expect the slope to strengthen beyond −2 with alpha holding near −6.5% and Sharpe near −0.58. This is my primary candidate for a signal that is strong on both criteria.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: EqualWeightCapStockAndDepAdequacyZ
EXPRESSION: ADD(ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent))), ZSCORE(MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), at), RATIO(TS_SUM(dp, 3), TS_SUM(capx, 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Accruals scaled by productive capital and accruals weighted by depreciation-versus-capex shortfall are complementary measurements of accounting growth, and an equal-weight standardized average should sit at the most attractive point of the alpha–slope trade-off.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The 2:1 tilt toward the alpha limb produced α −6.9% with FMB −1.65 and the archive's best Sharpe (−0.602), while the pure slope limb reaches FMB −3.91 with α −3.7%, and every composite so far has interpolated nearly linearly in the weights; equal weighting is therefore the natural next point and should land near α −6% with FMB around −2.4. This is the correct experiment to run last because it settles the weighting question with a directly comparable design rather than a new mechanism. Both limbs are dense and share the same three-year horizon, so no coverage or stability cost is incurred.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: DoubleBoundedAmplifiedCapStockAccruals
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent)), RATIO(TS_SUM(dp, 3), TS_SUM(ADD(capx, dp), 3))), RATIO(SUB(at, ADD(ppent, che)), at))
HYPOTHESIS: The most reversal-prone firms satisfy three conditions at once: large accruals relative to productive capital, gross investment that is almost entirely replacement, and a balance sheet dominated by soft, discretionary assets in which the overstatement can be parked.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Both amplifiers are bounded in roughly [0,1] and dense across the universe, which is precisely the condition that separated the successful dp/capx and soft-asset amplifiers from the sparse intangible amplifier that destroyed portfolio spread; the soft-asset amplifier previously moved a base signal's slope from −0.54 to −2.03 at a cost of 2.6 points of alpha. Stacking two mild bounded amplifiers on the strongest base tests whether slope gains accumulate faster than alpha decays, which the single-amplifier evidence suggests. If it overshoots into low alpha, signal 1 remains the preferred version of this idea, so the pair is jointly informative.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: CapStockScaledExpansionDeficit
EXPRESSION: RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ADD(capx, aqc), oancf), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent))
HYPOTHESIS: Three years of expansion — organic plus acquired — funded beyond operating cash flow, measured against the productive capital the firm actually operates, identifies growth that was financed rather than earned and has no capital base to sustain it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This fills the one untested cell in the archive's two-dimensional design space: the funding-deficit numerator owns the strongest and most consistent Fama-MacBeth slopes (−2.8 to −3.4 across five variants) while the capital-stock denominator owns the strongest alphas (−6.4% to −7.4%), and they have never been combined. Because the deficit numerator is monotone through the middle of the cross-section where the accrual-intensity numerator is flat, this is the most plausible route to a signal with both FMB near −3 and alpha near −6%. Coverage should be near 0.080 given the aqc limb, acceptable relative to the leaders.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: NonCashRecognitionPerProductiveCapital
EXPRESSION: RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), SUB(intan, LAG(intan, 3))), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent))
HYPOTHESIS: Accounting growth encompasses all non-cash recognition, so three years of accruals plus three years of intangible-asset accumulation, measured against productive capital, is a broader and more faithful measure of balance-sheet expansion by recognition rather than expenditure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Pooling intangible accumulation with accruals earned a respectable slope (FMB −2.41) on the older gross-investment denominator, and its slope contribution is economically independent of the depreciation-adequacy channel used in signals 1 through 3, so this broadens the mechanism rather than reweighting it. Adding the intangible limb inside the numerator, rather than multiplying by a sparse intangible amplifier, avoids the point-mass failure that destroyed IntangibleParkedDeficit's portfolio spread — firms without intangibles simply contribute zero to one numerator term instead of collapsing the whole signal. It is the batch's distinct mechanism and directly tests whether recognition generally, not accruals specifically, drives the reversal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: DualAccrualMeasurementCapStockZ
EXPRESSION: ADD(ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent))), ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), ppent))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-flow-statement accruals and balance-sheet non-cash working capital accruals are two independent measurements of the same economic quantity, so averaging them on the winning capital-stock scale should cancel measurement error and strengthen both forms of evidence.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: On the identical denominator the total-accrual numerator delivers α −7.4% with FMB −0.90 while the working-capital numerator delivers FMB −2.12 with the archive's best coverage (0.112), so their disagreement is a measurement issue rather than an economic one and averaging exploits exactly that. Unlike the amplifier route, this seeks a better slope without deliberately sacrificing alpha, since both limbs are alpha-bearing on this scale. It also provides the most robust fallback for out-of-sample use because it leans on two independent data sources and the widest coverage in the archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
